picks.title: Steam study of over 53,000 games finds "60-90% of the growth" in monthly releases is from games using AI - and almost none of them make money
picks.excerpt: A study of 53,597 Steam releases (July 2023-July 2026) finds AI-flagged games now drive the overwhelming majority of monthly-release growth - up to ~530 new titles a month - yet make almost none of the sales (33% of releases, ~10% of revenue in Q2 2026). A hard data snapshot of how generative tooling is reshaping game production volume and storefront economics.
picks.rationale: Hard data on how AI is flooding Steam volume without earning revenue - directly reframes how designers weigh generative pipelines against discoverability.

picks.title: Sony says AI is "exciting," great for "synthetic assets," and an "important foundational technology supporting our strategy"
picks.excerpt: PlayStation leadership frames AI - including 'synthetic assets' generated for game development - as a foundational pillar of Sony's strategy, spanning production efficiency, player experience and content discovery. A major first-party publisher openly committing to generative asset pipelines signals how AI is moving into AAA workflows.
picks.rationale: A top-tier first-party publisher publicly committing to synthetic-asset pipelines signals AI is now sanctioned inside AAA production workflows.

picks.title: An iOS Developer Vibe-Coded A "Capybara Food Delivery" Game Using Claude Code, 27,000 Lines Made Entirely By AI, And Won $25,000
picks.excerpt: A developer built and shipped a full mobile game whose ~27,000 lines of code were generated entirely by Claude Code through 'vibe coding,' taking a $25,000 contest prize. A concrete case study of an end-to-end AI-authored game, showing how far prompt-driven development has moved beyond assistive autocomplete.
picks.rationale: A concrete, awarded case study of an end-to-end AI-authored game - a tangible benchmark of what prompt-driven development can now ship.
